subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Jared Ortiz <jared@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Jul 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Hi Jared — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Summary:
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + suggested replies for tier-1 agents.
- Volume: ~120k monthly conversational turns, peak concurrency ~40 requests/sec.
- PII/redaction: several fields must be redacted (SSNs, payment tokens) before sending to hosted endpoints.

Next steps I promised:
1) Collect a representative prompt set from your team (edge cases included) so our SRE/SEs can run model-fit evals.
2) Share our recommended model candidates and benchmark links.
3) Outline redaction guidance and a short plan for privacy controls.

I've attached a lightweight prompt collection template (redwood_prompt_template.csv) to speed things up. If it's easier you can drop a few real examples (redact PII) or send a CSV.

Could you confirm who should own the prompt export on your side (content ops / product)? If you can get a first pass to me by EOD Monday (07/13) we can scope the eval and share preliminary model recommendations by the following week.

Attaching: redwood_prompt_template.csv (template)

Thanks — looking forward to iterating.

\u0014
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
Schedule a follow-up: https://calendly.com/logan-redwood/30

I'll try to get the file to you Monday.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Great — thanks for the quick reply, Jared. Short answers and what we'll do next: 

Redaction guidance:
- Placeholder [REDACTED] is fine for initial evals. Please avoid substituting with fake/real-looking values.
- For anything that might be a structured token (payment token, SSN), keep the format (e.g., ####-####) but replace digits with Xs so we can validate token parsing if needed.

Recommended models (initial shortlist):
- redwood-large-v1 (quantized): best latency/cost balance for long context summaries.
- redwood-chat-medium: strong for conversational turn-level replies, lower cost.
- open-llama-30b-finetuned: fallback candidate for high-accuracy scoring on niche jargon.

We've run preliminary benchmarks for similar customers — see linked report and our internal eval harness. We'll run your prompt set through the same pipelines and return: accuracy-likelihood metrics, hallucination spot checks, latency p50/p95, and token-cost estimates.

Attaching: redwood_eval_report_q1.pdf (sample benchmark for comparable workload)
Related: https://redwood.ai/docs/benchmarks/acme-model-fit

Marissa — could you take point on the eval run once Jared's file arrives? If we see quality regressions on generated summaries, we'll propose a short A/B with a tuned prompt set and a canary rollout on Dedicated capacity.

Jared — if you can share the CSV (or a GDrive link) by EOD Monday we'll prioritize the eval and aim to deliver a model-fit summary by 07/17.

Thanks,
Logan
\u0014\u0014
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jared Ortiz <jared@acme.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt set collection & model-fit next steps (Acme)

Hi Jared — looping in here as your SE. Quick checklist for the prompt export to make the eval fast and actionable:

Please include:
- Column A: user_message (raw user utterance, redact PII per Logan's guidance)
- Column B: agent_context (previous 2 turns, optional)
- Column C: expected_output (what a good reply would look like) — if you don't have ground truth, leave blank and we'll run human eval sampling.
- Column D: problem_tags (billing, cancellation, product-bug) — helps slice metrics
- Flag edge cases: intentionally short messages, multi-intent, code snippets, non-English phrases

If you expect any HIPAA/regulated content let us know explicitly so we can propose Private deployment options. For now, the hosted eval (with placeholders) is fine.

I will:
- Run the prompt set through our eval harness (redwood_eval_report_q1.pdf is an example).
- Surface any quality regressions vs. baseline and propose tuned prompt recipes.
- Recommend model + quantization profile that balances latency and accuracy for your SLA.

If you run into trouble exporting, you can paste a redacted sample (10-20 rows) directly into the body of an email and we'll start there.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

\u0014
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[internal eval harness] https://redwood.ai/internal/eval-harness
